subject: Capacity underwriting questionnaire & warm-start assumptions for ClearPath AI
messages:
From: Aline Guerrero <aline@clearpath.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity data + initial questions for Dedicated underwriting

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this week. As we scope ClearPath's Dedicated deployment, the procurement team wants an underwriting packet that ties expected user traffic to GPU footprint and a clear note on warm-start behavior (how session cache / KV reuse impacts effective concurrency). Attached is a small export of our traffic for the last 30 days and an example prompt mix.

Quick context:
- Production ML calls today (staging traffic appended) average ~18 reqs/sec during PST business hours but spike to ~240 reqs/sec during promo windows.
- Session model: we keep user sessions alive for up to 30 minutes; most sessions make repeated short requests (25–40 tokens prompts) with 1–3 generation calls each.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 400ms for short completions; p99 < 800ms for long prompt generations.

Can you confirm the specific data points you need so we provide a clean underwriting sheet? Also: what assumptions do you use for warm-start (KV cache hit rate, session pooling) when mapping to GPU count?

Attachments: clearpath_traffic_profile.csv (csv)

Thanks,
Aline
Head of Integrations
ClearPath AI
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Aline Guerrero <aline@clearpath.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity data + initial questions for Dedicated underwriting

Hi Aline —

Appreciate the export, that helps. I've attached a short underwriting template and a notes PDF that explain our warm-start modeling. Can you fill the yellow fields in the spreadsheet and return? Key pieces we need to size a Dedicated pool and map to a GPU SKU are below — filling these will let us give a firm slot estimate and a recommended oversubscription guardrail: 

- Average prompt token length (tokens) per request (weighted by call volume).
- Average response tokens per generation (tokens). If you use streaming, indicate percent of calls streamed.
- Average requests per active session and session TTL (you mentioned ~30m, please confirm).
- Peak concurrent active sessions during a promo (p95/p99 if available).
- Typical model(s) used (e.g., redwood-13b-q4, rwx-70b), and what percent of traffic each model represents.
- Acceptable tail latency (p95/p99) and whether you prefer throughput-first or latency-first sizing.

For warm-start assumptions we typically model three cache tiers:
- Cold start (no KV cache): cold_start_fraction = X%
- Warm session reuse (same session, KV in GPU local cache): kv_hit_rate = Y%
- Cross-session prefix cache (heuristic reuse for templated prompts): prefix_cache_hit = Z%

Default conservative values we use when unknown: cold_start_fraction=30%, kv_hit_rate=45%, prefix_cache_hit=5%. If you have telemetry on cache hits in your staging environment we can plug the real numbers and often reduce GPU needs by 20–40% for chat-like apps.

I added a few sample rows in the spreadsheet and sketched a sample compute mapping that shows how 1k concurrent prompt-generation-equivalent slots maps to GPUs for 2 different SKUs. Once you return the completed sheet we'll run a short sensitivity analysis and propose a Dedicated pool configuration + autoscale/burst knobs.

Attachments: redwood_underwriting_template.xlsx (xlsx), preflight-notes.pdf (pdf)

Next steps: please return the completed sheet (yellow fields) and any additional telemetry you have on session reuse and percent streaming. If easier, we can do a 30-min data handoff call Friday.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Aline Guerrero <aline@clearpath.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity data + initial questions for Dedicated underwriting

Karthik —

Thanks — attaching the CSV export we discussed and a quick answers doc. Highlights filled:
- avg_prompt_tokens: 78
- avg_response_tokens: 210 (approx 65% of calls require full generation; 35% are short lookups ~30 tokens)
- session_ttl: 30m, avg_requests_per_session: 2.4
- promo_peak_p95_concurrent_sessions: 1,100; promo_peak_p99_concurrent_sessions: 1,850
- model mix: rwd-13b-q4 (60%), rwd-33b (30%), rwd-70b (10%)
- streaming: 18% of calls are streaming, primarily for longer responses
- telemetry on KV/phrase reuse: estimated kv_hit_rate ~52%, prefix reuse ~8%

We returned the attached clearpath_traffic_profile.csv for the last 30 days. Let me know if you want the last 90 days as well.

Thanks,
Aline

---
Attachment: clearpath_traffic_profile_filled.csv (csv)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: draft underwriting assumptions for ClearPath (do not forward)

Karthik / Ben —

I reviewed Aline's returns. Good signal. Quick thoughts before we run a sensitivity pass:

1) Use Aline's KV hit numbers (kv_hit_rate 52%, prefix_reuse 8%) as our baseline. That reduces the effective concurrent gen-equivalent by roughly 42% relative to cold starts.
2) For mixed-model footprints assume: rwd-13b maps to 1.0x slot cost, rwd-33b ~2.8x, rwd-70b ~5.6x (these are our current engine figures for p99 latency targets). We'll include a model-mix weighted multiplier in the template.
3) Promo protection: propose reserving a dedicated 40% burst headroom (autoscale-burst) for two hours around expected promo windows.
4) Billing note: client asked for underwriting greenlines; we should prepare an ops note describing warm-cache performance variability and potential need for extra reserved capacity for the first 30 days of production.

Asks: Ben, can you run the quick GPU-mapping that converts Aline's p99 concurrent -> slot-equivalent and then to GPU counts for the two candidate SKUs (A100-80GB equiv and H100-80GB equiv)? I sketched an approach in the shared drive doc.

Marissa
Director, Pre-Sales
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Aline Guerrero <aline@clearpath.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity data + initial questions for Dedicated underwriting

Thanks all — quick summary and calendar invite attached.

Summary: using the provided traffic and Aline's cache telemetry, baseline Dedicated pool required to meet p99 targets (with 40% promo buffer) is:
- conservative SKU (A100-80GB equiv): 14 GPUs (with autoscale burst up to 20 for promo windows)
- performance SKU (H100-80GB equiv): 8 GPUs (autoscale burst up to 12)

Assumptions used: avg_prompt 78 tokens, avg_response 210 tokens, model-weighted slot multiplier 1.88, kv_hit_rate 52%, prefix_reuse 8%, cold_start_fraction 18%. Latency-first sizing at p99.

Next step: 30-min handoff call to walk through the workbook and confirm ops/SLAs. I scheduled a slot: https://calendar.redwood.com/meetings/clearpath-underwriting-30m (Fri 16 Mar 2028 11:00 PST). If that doesn't work, suggest two alternatives and we'll adapt.

Attachment: underwriting-summary.pdf (pdf)

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
